title: refactor(website): Play and Community on the v2 design system
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Part of #14472. Moves the last two old pages onto the v2 design system. The copy stays the same; #16103 changes copy.

- Restyles Play with v2's hero, page card and closing scene. The model picker, generator and user menu now use `@pollinations/ui` parts. All logic is unchanged.
- Restyles Community the same way: leaderboard, contributors, build diary and supporters. Fetching, translation and diary navigation are unchanged.
- Adds the Play and Community illustrations (day and night) from v2.
- Deletes the legacy Tailwind theme (`tailwind.config.ts`, the `@config` line), the old `ui/components/ui/*` parts, `palette.ts` and 6 dependencies that v2 also dropped.
- Shrinks the diff against `feat/website-v2` from 114 to 78 files.

Verified locally:
- Biome, tsc, 66 tests and the build pass.
- Every copy key is still used, and the visible text matches before and after. Tooltips were checked by hovering.
- Play generates an image. Community loads in light and dark mode.
- Nothing scrolls sideways at 390px.

The website deploy is paused (#16121), so this doesn't reach production yet.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: Two pages join the garden
gist.blurb: Play and Community get the v2 look, complete with day-and-night illustrations. The buttons moved house; image generation, leaderboards, and the words on the page stayed put.
gist.summary: Play and Community move to the v2 design system with new hero, page-card, and closing scenes, day-and-night illustrations, and shared @pollinations/ui controls, while their copy and behavior stay the same.
gist.impact: Visitors get a consistent v2 design across Play’s generator and model picker and Community’s leaderboard, contributors, build diary, and supporters, with no change to how those features work.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Play and Community as two neighboring spaces in a cozy digital garden, each with matching v2 page cards and a day-to-night illustration. Polli carries a tiny paintbrush between them; a small CRT monitor robot tends the image generator, while flowers frame the community board. The visual change is the point, not a new capability.
